summary:
To address the challenge of creating a space mission simulator for junior astronauts, the Kepler 186f Chivas team developed ORBIT (vcrorbit.com), an educational game designed from a child's creative perspective with the support of responsible adults.
The simulator challenges players to analyze and select the best materials to build their spacecraft, manage critical supplies for the mission's duration, and follow strict instructions before their limited oxygen runs out.
This project is important because it transforms purposeless screen time into meaningful, active learning. Instead of spending hours on aimless online games, children develop discipline, critical thinking, and time-management skills while having fun across different space missions. Furthermore, ORBIT ensures safe and universal accessibility: it is 100% free, requires no email registration, and can be played directly with an internet connection at vcrorbit.com.
details:
Project Development:

 

My project aims to create an interactive space mission simulation. In this experience, users must follow mission orders, manage limited supplies, and configure their own spacecraft. This puts their knowledge of space to the test while fostering an awareness that every resource we use—such as water, food, or plants—is vital; if these resources run out, everything comes to an end.

 

I will develop this using AI—specifically, Canva’s AI tools.

 

Prompt for the mission design phase:

 

A game in which participants must design their own spacecraft, configuring it to meet the specific requirements of various space missions. Participants have a set amount of time and must apply their knowledge of space to complete the mission, all while managing a limited supply of resources for the duration of the mission.

 

Prompt for the resource management phase:

 

An interactive game for a general audience where, during a space mission, astronauts must manage limited supplies over a specific period, as dictated by their assigned mission.

 

Prompt for the mission execution phase:

 

An interactive game in which the participant must carry out a space mission—such as collecting soil samples from the Moon—by following instructions within a set timeframe.

Disclaimer: as a first project, we effort to respect autors and copy rights lawyers.
